channel.title: Digital Assets Morning Wire
channel.description: Daily digital-asset regulatory and market digest. AI-sourced and AI-generated — verify against official sources before acting.

item.title: Michael Saylor teases ‘another color’ after four straight weeks without a Strategy bitcoin buy
item.description: Strategy (formerly MicroStrategy) executive chairman Michael Saylor hinted at new corporate financial activity after four consecutive weeks without the company adding to its bitcoin holdings. So what: A pause in one of the largest corporate bitcoin holders' buying pattern is primarily a market-watching item, though functions tracking counterparty crypto-treasury exposure may note any change in direction once details emerge. [single source]

item.title: 2 weeks left for Clarity: State of Crypto
item.description: The US Senate faces a tight deadline to advance the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act before its August recess, with a newly merged committee text that for the first time includes ethics provisions on the president's personal cryptocurrency dealings, though Democrats and Republicans still disagree on how strict those provisions should be. So what: The bill's market-structure provisions remain unsettled and contingent on resolving the ethics dispute, so a compliance function should continue treating a finalised US digital-asset market-structure law as not yet in place rather than planning around a specific outcome. [single source]

item.title: Europe's high regulatory bar could spark new crypto industry M&A wave
item.description: High compliance costs under the European Union's Markets in Crypto-Assets framework and the United Kingdom's developing crypto rules may push smaller crypto firms toward mergers with, or acquisition by, traditional financial institutions that already have the required governance, capital and custody systems in place. So what: As compliance-driven consolidation brings more crypto activity inside regulated financial institutions' ownership structures, due-diligence processes for new banking relationships and counterparties should expect more crypto-native firms to appear as acquisition targets or subsidiaries of traditional financial groups. [single source]

item.title: EU adds HTX to Russia sanctions list, barring transactions starting Aug. 23
item.description: The European Union added the crypto exchange HTX (formerly Huobi) to its Russia sanctions list as part of its 21st sanctions package, barring European Union operators from transacting with the platform from 23 August 2026, though eligible European Union, European Economic Area and Swiss nationals have a wind-down window to withdraw funds or close accounts. So what: Sanctions and crypto-counterparty screening lists should be updated to include HTX ahead of the 23 August 2026 effective date, and any existing exposure to the platform should be reviewed given the limited wind-down window for European Union, European Economic Area and Swiss account holders. [corroborated]

item.title: North Korea arrests hackers accused of laundering stolen funds from country's bank via crypto
item.description: North Korea's own intelligence agency arrested former military hackers accused of stealing foreign-currency and trade funds from two North Korean state banks and laundering them through cryptocurrency and China-based brokers before the scheme was detected. So what: The laundering techniques described, splitting transfers into small amounts, using encrypted messaging and unregistered devices, and converting through brokers near the China border, match patterns already associated with North Korea-linked crypto theft more broadly, making this a useful reference point for transaction-monitoring typologies. [single source]

item.title: Bitcoin ETF weekly trading volume falls to lowest since October 2024 as ether funds lead inflows again
item.description: Weekly trading volume for United States spot bitcoin exchange-traded funds fell to its lowest level since October 2024, while ether funds continued to attract more new inflows than bitcoin funds. So what: Declining bitcoin ETF trading activity alongside continued ether fund inflows is a market-structure trend worth noting for functions that monitor product concentration and flows through regulated fund wrappers, though it does not itself change any compliance obligation. [single source]

item.title: Outcomes monitoring: why understanding the consumer experience matters and where firms should focus
item.description: The UK Financial Conduct Authority published guidance on outcomes monitoring under its Consumer Duty framework, calling on regulated firms to track whether customers are actually experiencing good results from products and services, not just collect data passively. So what: The piece does not address digital assets directly, but its emphasis on evidencing real customer outcomes, not just monitoring activity, is a supervisory expectation that could extend to firms offering crypto-adjacent retail products under the same Consumer Duty framework. [official]

item.title: NY Attorney General Letitia James warns Clarity Act would ‘dilute’ states’ ability to go after fraud as pressure mounts
item.description: New York Attorney General Letitia James testified to the US Senate that the pending Digital Asset Market Clarity Act would preempt state investor-protection laws and weaken states' ability to prosecute cryptocurrency fraud, and called for stronger anti-money-laundering, know-your-customer and anti-mixing-service requirements in the bill. So what: The dispute over whether federal crypto market-structure legislation should preempt state enforcement powers remains unresolved, so a compliance function should continue monitoring both federal and state-level crypto enforcement activity rather than assuming one will supersede the other soon. [single source]

item.title: Securitize expands regulated platform with SEC adviser license
item.description: Securitize Capital, a subsidiary of the tokenisation platform Securitize, registered with the US Securities and Exchange Commission as an investment adviser, adding to its existing SEC-registered broker-dealer and transfer-agent registrations. So what: The registration lets Securitize work directly with asset managers and institutional investors on tokenised investment strategies under a regulated framework, so counterparties evaluating tokenisation service providers should note this adds to the small set of platforms holding a full stack of US federal securities registrations. [corroborated]

item.title: Metaplanet’s brokerage deal ‘badly undersells’ plans for bitcoin-backed ‘Bitbonds,’ Benchmark says
item.description: An analyst at Benchmark said Metaplanet's recent brokerage acquisition undersells the company's broader plans for bitcoin-backed bond products it calls "Bitbonds." So what: This is analyst commentary on a corporate strategy, not a regulatory development, though functions tracking bitcoin-backed debt instruments as an emerging product category may want to note Metaplanet's plans. [single source]

item.title: IBM portfolio acquisition makes Circle the largest US blockchain patent holder
item.description: Circle, the issuer of the USDC stablecoin, acquired a portfolio of blockchain-related patents from IBM, making it the largest holder of blockchain patents among US companies. So what: A stablecoin issuer building a large patent portfolio is a competitive and intellectual-property development rather than a compliance matter, though it may be useful context for functions assessing a major stablecoin issuer's overall business position. [single source]

item.title: Thailand's SEC alleges Bitkub concealed cyberattack that led to $50 million hack
item.description: Thailand's Securities and Exchange Commission alleged that the cryptocurrency exchange Bitkub and two of its former directors concealed a 2021 cyberattack that resulted in the theft of digital assets worth about 50 million US dollars, and filed a criminal complaint over the alleged concealment. So what: This is a reminder that concealing a security incident from a securities regulator can itself become a separate enforcement matter years later, so incident-disclosure obligations to regulators should be treated as an ongoing requirement, not a one-time judgment call made at the time of the breach. [corroborated]

item.title: Circle buys nearly 1,000 blockchain patents from IBM
item.description: Circle, the issuer of the USDC stablecoin, purchased close to 1,000 blockchain-related patents from IBM. So what: This patent acquisition is a competitive and intellectual-property development rather than a compliance matter, though it may be useful context for functions assessing a major stablecoin issuer's overall business position. [single source]

item.title: Kraken parent Payward acquires Magic Labs’ embedded wallet business
item.description: Payward, the parent company of the Kraken cryptocurrency exchange, acquired the embedded-wallet business of Magic Labs. So what: This is a corporate acquisition expanding Kraken's wallet infrastructure, not a regulatory development, though it may be useful context for functions assessing counterparty group structures. [single source]

item.title: Michael Saylor's Strategy boosted cash reserve to $3.75 billion, repurchased $25 million of STRC
item.description: Strategy (formerly MicroStrategy) increased its cash reserve to 3.75 billion US dollars and repurchased 25 million US dollars of its own stock. So what: Changes in a major corporate bitcoin holder's cash position and share buybacks are market and balance-sheet developments rather than compliance matters, though functions tracking counterparty financial health may note the shift. [single source]

item.title: Bitcoin ETFs post third straight weekly inflows despite $465 million in late-week losses
item.description: US spot bitcoin exchange-traded funds recorded a third consecutive week of net inflows overall, despite 465 million US dollars in losses during the final days of the week. So what: Continued net inflows into regulated bitcoin fund products is a market-structure trend worth noting for functions that monitor product concentration and flows through regulated fund wrappers, though it does not itself change any compliance obligation. [single source]

item.title: Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong criticizes crypto startups that rebrand to AI
item.description: Coinbase chief executive Brian Armstrong publicly criticised crypto startups that have been rebranding themselves as artificial-intelligence companies. So what: This is public commentary and industry opinion rather than a regulatory or compliance development, with no direct action required. [single source]

item.title: Interest rates in U.S., U.K., Japan and Coinbase, Strategy earnings: Crypto Week Ahead
item.description: A weekly market preview covered upcoming interest-rate decisions in the United States, United Kingdom and Japan alongside earnings reports from Coinbase and Strategy. So what: This is a market-calendar roundup rather than a regulatory development, useful only as a general awareness item of upcoming market-moving events. [single source]

item.title: South Korea’s KB Kookmin Bank to launch cross-border payment service on JPMorgan’s Kinexys: report
item.description: South Korea's KB Kookmin Bank will launch a cross-border payment service built on JPMorgan's blockchain-based Kinexys platform. So what: This is another example of an established bank using blockchain-based payment infrastructure for cross-border settlement, a trend worth tracking as more banks integrate similar rails into correspondent banking relationships. [single source]

item.title: The Funding: Are crypto vaults funds and curators fund managers?
item.description: A US Securities and Exchange Commission commissioner raised the question of whether decentralised-finance "vaults" -- pooled onchain contracts that deploy deposits under a stated strategy -- and their curators fall under existing US securities laws as unregistered investment funds and fund managers. So what: Curated vaults hold billions of dollars in assets and the applicable rules remain unsettled, so a compliance function should treat this as an emerging, still-unresolved area of United States securities regulation to monitor rather than a settled classification. [single source]

item.title: Strengthening resilience across an increasingly interconnected financial system
item.description: The UK Financial Conduct Authority explained its new Critical Third Parties oversight regime, which directly monitors essential technology and service providers supporting the UK financial system after finding that 27 percent of incidents reported to it in 2025 involved third-party issues. So what: The piece does not address digital assets directly, but its focus on systemic third-party operational risk is a supervisory approach that could extend to critical infrastructure providers digital-asset firms also rely on, such as custody technology or cloud services. [official]

item.title: GDF and ISDA Release Landmark Report on U.S. Tokenized Money Market Funds
item.description: Global Digital Finance and the International Swaps and Derivatives Association published a report, based on sandbox testing by 48 firms and survey responses from over 120 financial institutions, concluding that tokenised money market funds can function as institutional collateral under existing United States law, with two exceptions. So what: With most surveyed institutions planning to launch tokenised money market funds and to accept them as collateral within the next two years, functions handling collateral and counterparty due diligence should expect tokenised fund structures to become a more common feature of institutional relationships. [official]

item.title: Crypto hacks hit record high in H1 2026 as losses top $1 billion, Blockaid says
item.description: Blockchain security firm Blockaid reported that crypto hacks and exploits reached a record number of incidents in the first half of 2026, with total losses exceeding 1 billion US dollars, of which nearly 600 million US dollars was linked to North Korean hacking groups. So what: The continued concentration of theft losses in North Korea-linked incidents, often carried out via social-engineering attacks on multi-signature wallet holders, reinforces the value of screening counterparties and transaction patterns against known North Korea-linked typologies. [single source]

item.title: BlackRock, Fidelity, other Wall Street giants back the Clarity Act
item.description: BlackRock, Fidelity, Franklin Templeton, Goldman Sachs and SoFi publicly endorsed the pending Digital Asset Market Clarity Act, while the bill's path through the US Senate remains constrained by limited floor time before the chamber's August recess. So what: Broad Wall Street support does not resolve the bill's unsettled ethics provisions or guarantee timely passage, so a compliance function should continue treating US digital-asset market-structure legislation as pending rather than final. [single source]

item.title: Russia outlines new digital depository rules ahead of fall crypto framework roll-out
item.description: Russia's central bank published draft rules establishing regulated "digital depositories" to hold and record cryptocurrency and other digital-asset holdings, with tiered minimum capital requirements depending on the type of custody or settlement activity, ahead of a broader digital-assets law taking full effect by September 2026. So what: As Russia builds out a formal regulated custody framework for digital assets, due-diligence processes evaluating exposure to Russia-linked crypto infrastructure should track which entities become licensed digital depositories, particularly given the framework's timing alongside recent European Union sanctions on Russia-linked crypto platforms. [corroborated]

item.title: Morgan Stanley debuts Ethereum and Solana ETFs with market’s lowest fee, staking rewards
item.description: Morgan Stanley launched exchange-traded funds providing exposure to ether and solana, offering the lowest fees in the market along with staking rewards. So what: This is a peer financial institution's digital-asset product launch rather than a regulatory development, useful as context for functions tracking how mainstream brokers are expanding crypto product offerings. [single source]

item.title: Morgan Stanley debuts ether, solana exchange-traded products after bitcoin fund success
item.description: Morgan Stanley debuted ether and solana exchange-traded products following the earlier success of its bitcoin fund. So what: This is a peer financial institution's digital-asset product launch rather than a regulatory development, useful as context for functions tracking how mainstream brokers are expanding crypto product offerings. [single source]

item.title: Russia’s central bank drafts first rules for ‘organized’ crypto trading
item.description: Russia's central bank published its first draft rules for "organised" cryptocurrency trading venues, part of the broader digital-assets framework due to take full effect by September 2026. So what: As Russia moves toward licensing formal crypto trading venues, functions assessing counterparty and correspondent exposure to Russia-linked crypto infrastructure should track which platforms become licensed under the new framework. [single source]

item.title: Binance makes fighting crypto crime more difficult, says new report
item.description: The New York Times reported that Binance's April 2025 policy requiring most foreign law-enforcement data requests to be routed through the United Arab Emirates or formal mutual-legal-assistance treaties has significantly slowed investigators' ability to obtain user records and freeze or seize stolen assets, according to European and United States investigators; Binance disputes that its cooperation has slowed. So what: Counterparty and correspondent due-diligence assessments of exchanges should factor in how quickly a platform can respond to a legitimate law-enforcement or asset-freeze request, since slower response times can directly affect the ability to recover funds in a fraud or hack investigation. [single source]

item.title: Hong Kong’s central bank puts a number on lenders' quantum preparedness. It's very low.
item.description: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority found that Hong Kong's banking sector scored only 2.3 out of 10 on its newly created Quantum Preparedness Index, with about half of banks not yet having formal plans to transition to quantum-resistant cryptography ahead of an estimated threat window as early as 2029. So what: Because quantum computing threatens the same cryptographic foundations that secure digital-asset custody and blockchain transactions, a low industry-wide quantum-readiness score is directly relevant to assessing the long-term security of any digital-asset custody or wallet infrastructure a Hong Kong-linked counterparty relies on. [corroborated]

item.title: U.S. Senate puts off crypto Clarity Act for now as it focuses limited bandwidth elsewhere
item.description: The US Senate delayed further action on the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act to prioritise other business, including nominations and Russia sanctions legislation, before its 8 August summer recess, leaving the bill's ethics provisions for senior officials' personal crypto dealings still unresolved. So what: With the bill unlikely to advance before the recess and its next realistic window uncertain, a compliance function should continue planning around the absence of finalised US digital-asset market-structure legislation for the time being. [single source]

item.title: Fed holds rates steady as 3 officials push for hike while crypto market stays flat
item.description: The US Federal Reserve held its benchmark interest rate steady at 3.5 to 3.75 percent, with three policymakers dissenting in favour of a rate increase, citing Middle East-driven energy-price pressures on inflation; cryptocurrency prices were largely unmoved by the decision. So what: A steady-to-easier US interest-rate environment is a general market backdrop rather than a compliance development, though functions monitoring macro conditions affecting institutional crypto flows may note continued rate stability. [single source]

item.title: Visa CEO sidesteps labeling Open USD a challenger to Tether and USDC: ‘Our role is not to pick winners’
item.description: Visa's chief executive declined to characterise the company's new Open USD stablecoin initiative as a direct challenger to Tether or Circle's USDC, saying Visa's role is not to pick market winners. So what: This is corporate positioning commentary rather than a regulatory development, useful only as context for functions tracking how major payment networks are approaching stablecoin infrastructure. [single source]

item.title: Anchorage Digital says Fed’s proposed payment account is no ‘workable substitute’ for master account
item.description: Anchorage Digital filed a comment letter opposing the Federal Reserve's proposed limited "payment account" for crypto companies, arguing that excluding FedACH access, intraday liquidity and interest on reserves makes it an impractical substitute for a full Federal Reserve master account. So what: As long as crypto-native banks lack full, direct access to Federal Reserve payment infrastructure, they will continue relying on intermediary banks for settlement, which is a relevant factor when assessing a crypto-native counterparty's operational and concentration risk. [corroborated]

item.title: The traditional 9-to-5 banking day is officially dying, says Morgan Stanley execs
item.description: Morgan Stanley executives said the traditional nine-to-five banking day is ending as blockchain-based settlement and round-the-clock digital markets push financial institutions toward continuous operations. So what: As institutions move toward round-the-clock settlement, transaction-monitoring and sanctions-screening functions built around traditional business-day cycles may need to adapt to a continuous operating model. [single source]

item.title: Coinbase hit by spot trading slump: Wall Street trims expectations ahead of earnings
item.description: Wall Street analysts lowered earnings expectations for Coinbase ahead of its results, citing a slowdown in spot trading volume. So what: This is a market-performance and analyst-expectations item rather than a compliance development, useful only as general context on exchange business conditions. [single source]

item.title: ‘The moment to act is now’: Solana Policy Institute urges Senate to move on crypto bill as time dwindles
item.description: The Solana Policy Institute urged the US Senate to act on pending crypto market-structure legislation before time runs out in the current legislative session. So what: This is an industry advocacy position rather than a regulatory development, consistent with the continued uncertainty around when, or whether, US market-structure legislation will pass. [single source]

item.title: Tether’s GENIUS-compliant USAT stablecoin launches on Celo, marking first expansion beyond Ethereum
item.description: Tether's US-regulated USAT stablecoin, issued through the federally chartered Anchorage Digital Bank under the GENIUS Act framework, expanded to the Celo blockchain, marking its first deployment beyond Ethereum. So what: As GENIUS Act-compliant stablecoins expand across more blockchain networks, due-diligence and transaction-monitoring processes should track which chains and venues carry regulated, bank-issued stablecoins compared with unregulated alternatives. [corroborated]

item.title: The inside story of how a hike in Hong Kong changed crypto trading forever
item.description: A feature article recounted how BitMEX co-founder Ben Delo invented the perpetual swap, a futures contract with no expiry date, during a casual hike in Hong Kong in 2015; the product is now used by every major crypto exchange and processes tens of trillions of dollars in trading volume annually. So what: This is a product-history feature rather than a regulatory development, useful only as background on how perpetual swaps, a product now facing possible United States regulatory frameworks, originated. [single source]

item.title: How banks should approach stablecoin compliance and financial crime risk
item.description: Compliance analytics firm Elliptic published a framework for banks assessing stablecoin-related financial-crime risk, identifying three channels through which such risk can reach a bank (counterparty, product and indirect exposure) and five design factors that shape a given stablecoin's risk profile, including transferability, ecosystem participants, regulatory status, freezability and the extent of blockchain analytics use. So what: The framework's emphasis on verifying an issuer's actual on-chain wallet behaviour, not just its disclosed policies, is a practical due-diligence enhancement banks assessing stablecoin exposure or counterparty relationships may want to incorporate. [single source]

item.title: Bernstein cuts Circle price target to $140, says Open USD threat will fade
item.description: Investment bank Bernstein cut its price target for Circle, the issuer of the USDC stablecoin, to 140 US dollars, saying competitive pressure from Visa's Open USD initiative is likely to fade. So what: This is an analyst valuation call rather than a regulatory development, useful only as general market context on competitive dynamics among stablecoin issuers. [single source]

item.title: Binance offers gold and silver options after commodity futures pull in billions in daily volume
item.description: Binance launched options contracts on gold and silver after its existing commodity futures products attracted billions of dollars in daily trading volume. So what: This is a product-expansion item rather than a regulatory development, useful only as context on how major exchanges are broadening into traditional-commodity-linked derivatives. [single source]

item.title: The fall of A7A5: how sanctions strangled the ruble stablecoin
item.description: The A7A5 ruble-pegged stablecoin, designed to help Russia evade Western sanctions and first backed by a sanctioned Russian state bank, collapsed after the United States, United Kingdom and European Union designated it and its supporting infrastructure in 2025, with transaction volumes down 96 percent from their peak and no new tokens minted since July 2025. So what: This is a concrete case study showing that coordinated sanctions designations, combined with exchanges screening and freezing tainted funds, can materially shut down a sanctions-evasion vehicle even while its smart contracts remain technically operational, reinforcing the value of screening for exposure to designated stablecoins specifically, not just to designated entities directly. [corroborated]

item.title: Coinbase wants to be Canada’s ‘everything exchange,’ but says clearer rules are needed first
item.description: Coinbase said it wants to become Canada's comprehensive "everything exchange" but that clearer regulatory rules are needed first. So what: This is a corporate market-expansion statement rather than a regulatory development, useful only as context on how a major exchange is positioning for the Canadian market pending regulatory clarity. [single source]

item.title: Coinbase shares slip after Q2 results despite prediction markets doubling and record trading market share
item.description: Coinbase's stock fell about 7% in after-hours trading even though the exchange reported record global crypto trading market share and more than doubled its prediction-market revenue in the second quarter. So what: The drop despite strong operating metrics is a reminder that even leading regulated exchanges remain exposed to volatile investor sentiment, which is useful context when assessing the financial stability of exchange counterparties. [single source]

item.title: Coinbase sinks 5% after missing second quarter revenue estimates
item.description: Coinbase shares fell about 5% after the exchange reported second-quarter revenue of 1.22 billion dollars, roughly 70 million dollars below analyst estimates, as industry-wide crypto trading volumes fell more than 20 percent during the quarter. So what: A broad decline in industry trading volumes affecting even the largest exchange is a useful indicator when reviewing revenue and liquidity assumptions for exchange counterparties. [single source]

item.title: IRS warns crypto holders fraudster sending fake letters in attempt to steal digital assets or data: Bloomberg
item.description: The United States Internal Revenue Service warned that fraudsters are mailing fake letters to crypto holders directing them to a bogus 'Digital Asset Compliance Portal' in an attempt to steal digital assets or personal data. So what: The warning is useful input for customer fraud-awareness communications, since it shows criminals impersonating tax authorities by physical mail rather than only email or text, a channel account holders may trust more readily. [corroborated]

item.title: JPMorgan says crypto bill’s fading odds hurt outlook, warns parts could discourage institutional adoption
item.description: JPMorgan analysts said prediction-market odds that the United States Clarity Act crypto market-structure bill passes this year have fallen to their lowest point so far, and warned some provisions could let decentralised-finance platforms trade tokenised securities and derivatives entirely outside the oversight of the Securities and Exchange Commission or the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, while holding crypto firms to lighter anti-money-laundering standards than banks. So what: If the bill advances with those gaps intact, banks should expect an uneven anti-money-laundering standard between regulated institutions and crypto trading platforms, a live legislative uncertainty worth tracking when assessing digital-asset counterparties. [corroborated]

item.title: Global banks test tokenized money for cross-border payments in $1 million BIS pilot
item.description: Five central banks and 28 commercial banks, including JPMorgan, Citi, UBS, Deutsche Bank and Standard Chartered, completed a Bank for International Settlements pilot moving about 1 million dollars in tokenised central-bank and commercial-bank money across six currencies, with cross-border payments settling in around 80 seconds. So what: As major international banks gain live experience with tokenised, multi-currency settlement rails, compliance functions should expect tokenisation and real-time cross-border settlement to become a mainstream part of correspondent banking rather than a niche pilot. [corroborated]

item.title: The 2026 World Cup On-Chain: $20 Billion in Crypto Flows, From Bets to Tickets
item.description: Blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis reported that 2026 FIFA World Cup-linked prediction markets and digital-collectible ticketing generated around 20 billion dollars in on-chain activity, with less than 1 percent of prediction-market wallets showing ties to illicit activity, including 5.4 million dollars traced to the sanctioned exchange Huobi, also known as HTX. So what: The small but real flow of funds to a sanctioned exchange during a major global sporting event is a reminder to keep already-sanctioned virtual-asset platforms such as Huobi/HTX on watch-lists when reviewing customer transaction patterns around high-volume events. [single source]

item.title: JPMorgan says fading Clarity Act odds weigh on crypto outlook
item.description: CoinDesk reported that JPMorgan's research team now sees fading odds that the United States Congress passes the Clarity Act crypto market-structure bill this year, and flagged that parts of the bill could leave decentralised-finance trading outside the Securities and Exchange Commission and Commodity Futures Trading Commission's oversight while holding crypto firms to lighter anti-money-laundering obligations than banks and broker-dealers. So what: The same anti-money-laundering gap flagged across multiple outlets is a reason to read closely whatever final bill text emerges before relying on it to set risk-based due-diligence expectations for crypto-platform counterparties. [corroborated]

item.title: Bitcoin ETFs on track for the smallest monthly inflows ever
item.description: United States spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds attracted just 205 million dollars in net inflows in July, the lowest monthly total since they launched, reflecting weak institutional demand even as prices moved higher. So what: Thin institutional inflows into regulated Bitcoin investment products are a useful indicator of institutional risk appetite when calibrating expectations for digital-asset business volumes. [single source]

item.title: South Korea plans to tax crypto gains over $1,740 as political battle moves to parliament
item.description: South Korea's government confirmed plans to start taxing cryptocurrency gains above about 1,740 dollars at a combined 22 percent rate from January 2027, even as opposition lawmakers push a competing bill to scrap the tax entirely. So what: A confirmed effective date for retail crypto-gains taxation, alongside a live legislative push to repeal it, is useful context for anticipating shifts in customer trading activity toward offshore exchanges or peer-to-peer venues if the tax proceeds as planned. [corroborated]

item.title: Ostium blames off-chain breach for $24 million exploit, rules out smart contract flaw
item.description: Onchain derivatives exchange Ostium said attackers stole about 24 million dollars in USDC, a United States dollar-pegged stablecoin, by compromising its off-chain price-reporting infrastructure to submit false Bitcoin price data, and said the incident did not involve a smart-contract vulnerability or a compromise of the multi-signature wallets governing the protocol. So what: The incident is a reminder that a decentralised-finance protocol's on-chain code can be secure while its off-chain infrastructure remains a weak point, worth factoring into due-diligence on any digital-asset platform's operational risk controls. [single source]

item.title: Russia detains crypto mining firm BitRiver founder on fraud charges: report
item.description: Russian authorities detained Igor Runets, founder of the crypto-mining company BitRiver, on fraud charges relating to an equipment transaction with the energy group En+, and separately charged him with tax evasion. So what: BitRiver's Swiss holding company was added to the United States Treasury's sanctions list in 2022 for helping Russian entities evade sanctions through crypto mining, so continued developments involving its leadership remain useful input for ongoing due-diligence and sanctions-screening reviews of the group and its subsidiaries. [single source]

item.title: Binance.US to apply for CFTC license in August for prediction market platform
item.description: Binance.US said it plans to apply in August for a United States Commodity Futures Trading Commission licence that would let it offer futures, options and event-based prediction contracts to retail customers, entering a market already served by Kalshi and Polymarket US. So what: A major exchange seeking a federally regulated licence for prediction markets signals further convergence between crypto-exchange and traditional derivatives-market regulation, useful when assessing the regulatory maturity of exchange counterparties offering these products. [single source]

item.title: Senators ready to send stricter ethics rules on Trump's crypto ventures to White House, sources say
item.description: United States Senators Thom Tillis and Ruben Gallego finalised, but have not yet publicly detailed, revised ethics language meant to limit senior government officials' financial ties to crypto ventures, which still needs White House and Democratic sign-off before the Senate's self-described 'sell-by date' of 7 August to attach it to the Clarity Act. So what: Whether this ethics language survives into a final bill will shape how seriously government conflict-of-interest standards for crypto holdings are enforced, worth monitoring given the reputational sensitivity of dealing with politically exposed persons who hold digital assets. [single source]
